title: Window ignores size overrides when going out of fullscreen
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible: v4.7.2.stable.arch_linux [ed1daf0bf], v4.8.dev6.official [8898c2b3d]

### System information

Godot v4.7.2.stable (ed1daf0bf) - Arch Linux #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Mon, 14 Sep 2026 22:41:30 +0000 on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Mobile) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 (nvidia; 615.71.09) - AMD Ryzen 5 2600 Six-Core Processor (12 threads) - 31.28 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

If you set `display/window/size/window_width_override` and `display/window/size/window_height_override` values and start the game, the window is indeed set to this overridden size.

But if you start the game in `FULLSCREEN` and then go out of `FULLSCREEN into `WINDOWED` the screen height is smaller.

This is how I handle toggling fullscreen:
```
func toggle_fullscreen() -> void:
	if window_mode == DisplayServer.WindowMode.WINDOW_MODE_FULLSCREEN:
		window_mode = DisplayServer.WindowMode.WINDOW_MODE_WINDOWED
	elif window_mode != DisplayServer.WindowMode.WINDOW_MODE_FULLSCREEN:
		window_mode = DisplayServer.WindowMode.WINDOW_MODE_FULLSCREEN
	
	DisplayServer.window_set_mode(window_mode)

func _input(event: InputEvent) -> void:
	if event is InputEventKey:
		var key: InputEventKey = event as InputEventKey
		if key.keycode == KEY_F11 && !key.pressed:
			toggle_fullscreen()
```

Maybe this is an incorrect way to do this and that's why it happens?

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ffde7050-761f-4a98-8e8c-051cf2eaefcf

On a related note: I also found that I can't set the window's height to more than 1040px (I have a 1080p monitor). I'm quite certain that 40px is the taskbar height. I'm not sure if Godot doesn't not let me do that or it's the OS itself (so you don't hide the taskbar).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a project.
2. Add code above to a script.
3. Set window size overrides.
4. Set window to start WINDOWED and run the game. Check window height against the 2D ruler (on 100% zoom i.e. 1:1)
5. Set window to start WINDOWED and run the game. Check window height against the 2D ruler and see that the window's height is smaller.
